title: Rosalind and the Machine
premise: Quentin Okonkwo tends the Verdance, a terraforming garden seeded for colonists who never arrived, and keeps meticulous records of a settlement quietly failing around her. When she discovers an unfamiliar name — Rosalind — on the manifest of a ship that never flew, her investigation reveals that two rival fleets are held together by a fabricated truce built on that ghost entry. As factions close in on the truth, Quentin must keep Rosalind's fiction alive, giving the lie a face, a voice, and eventually a life of its own, until maintaining it costs her everything she loves. In the end she chooses truth over loyalty, releasing the lie at the truce's expiration and forcing both fleets to negotiate as what they actually are: survivors with nowhere else to go.
about_author: Dominic Halloran is the pen name of a former hydrologist who spent six years on remote research stations before turning to fiction. He writes about people who maintain impossible systems, and about the moment maintenance becomes mercy.

chapters.title: The Garden for No One
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She walks the Verdance, logging soil failures and nutrient drift while the colony above ground shrinks another dozen souls. A supply drone arrives carrying manifests for ships that never launched. Emotional beat: quiet devotion curdling into unease as she realizes someone is still filing paperwork for the dead.

chapters.title: A Name That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Quentin cross-references old fleet archives and finds 'Rosalind' appended to the manifest of the Meridian, a vessel destroyed before launch — or so history says. Her queries trigger an automated flag she doesn't recognize. POV shifts briefly to Fleet Archivist Sefa Iwu, who notices the query and hesitates over whether to report it. Beat: curiosity becoming complicity.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Sefa arrives at the colony under cover of a routine inspection and tells Quentin the truth: the truce between the Founders' Fleet and the Drift holds only because both sides believe Rosalind — supposedly a shared hostage-heir — exists aboard neutral territory. Quentin's records prove she was invented decades ago. Beat: vertigo; her garden is collateral in a peace built on nothing.

chapters.title: What the Records Keep
chapters.summary: Quentin digs into who forged the manifest and finds her own mentor, the late terraformer Amaechi, listed among the original conspirators. Flashbacks via recovered logs show Amaechi inventing Rosalind to stop a war the colonists couldn't survive. Beat: grief braided with reluctant admiration — the lie was an act of love.

chapters.title: Expiration Date
chapters.summary: Sefa reveals the truce renews only if both fleets' envoys can verify Rosalind at the next summit, ninety days out. The original forgers are dead or scattered. Quentin refuses; Sefa points out that exposure means mutual bombardment of the colony. Beat: trapped — justice outside the law now means perpetuating fraud.

chapters.title: Giving Her a Face
chapters.summary: Quentin builds Rosalind: a persona stitched from garden logs, Amaechi's letters, and a synthetic presence voiced through the Verdance's environmental systems. The found family of remaining colonists — engineer Bex, child Teo, medic Oyelaran — each contribute pieces without fully knowing why. Beat: warmth and dread intertwined; the lie starts feeling like a person.

chapters.title: The Envoy's Visit
chapters.summary: POV alternates between Quentin and Drift envoy Cass Meric, who interviews 'Rosalind' through the greenhouse glass. Cass leaves half-convinced but plants a tracker. Bex is caught tampering with it and detained. Beat: first real cost — loyalty demanding sacrifice from the innocent.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Teo, having pieced together the truth, confronts Quentin: Rosalind has his dead sister's name, taken from Amaechi's memorial wall. The found family splinters; Oyelaran threatens to broadcast everything unless Quentin ends it. Meanwhile Cass's tracker data reaches hardliners on both fleets. Beat: the lie devouring its keepers.

chapters.title: Ninety Days
chapters.summary: At the summit verification, Quentin appears as Rosalind herself — the gardener as the ghost — and delivers a speech woven from Amaechi's logs, confessing the fabrication to both fleets simultaneously rather than let one side weaponize it. Hardliners move to strike; Sefa and Cass, each betraying their own chain of command, stall the launch codes. Beat: climax — truth offered as the only remaining act of loyalty.

chapters.title: Planting Season
chapters.summary: In the aftermath, the fleets, stripped of the truce's fiction, negotiate a rawer pact over shared resources — anchored by the Verdance itself, now designated common ground. Quentin returns to her garden with Bex, Teo, and Oyelaran reconciled but changed, and adds Rosalind to the memorial wall not as a lie but as everyone the colony lost. Beat: bittersweet resolution — justice grown, not decreed.
